Group definition for GroupKFold (33033 groups): dataset rows -> `<csv file>:<original row id>`; extracted fragments inherit the group of the statement they were cut from; template-generated payloads -> attack-template id (21 templates); synthetic benign inputs -> generator-template id (12 templates). Whole templates are therefore held out together.

## 8 External dataset (Table IV)

**Dataset: CSIC 2010 HTTP dataset** (Giménez, Villegas & Álvarez Marañón, CSIC 2010). Copy used: https://github.com/msudol/Web-Application-Attack-Datasets (CSVData/csic_final.csv). 61,065 requests = 36,000 valid + 25,065 anomalous. Confirm the dataset's own terms of use on the CSIC page before citing a licence (the GitHub mirror's GPL-3.0 covers the converter, not necessarily the data).

Protocol (run once, no tuning on this data; models = the final fits on the full training set): each request is reduced to what the API guard would inspect (query-string and form-body VALUES; not the URL path, headers or cookies), values are decoded once (as the framework does) and then passed through `normalize()`; a request is flagged if ANY value scores >= 0.5. Positive class = CSIC label `Anomalous`.

**Table IV — CSIC 2010 (request level, %)**

| Model | Accuracy | F1 | FPR | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Random Forest | 64.29 | 23.03 | 0.02 | 99.82 | 13.01 |
| XGBoost | 66.01 | 30.67 | 0.78 | 94.25 | 18.31 |

All models (same protocol):

| Model | Acc | F1 | FPR (all valid) | FPR (valid w/ fields) | Recall (all anomalous) | Recall (anomalous w/ fields) | Recall (SQLi-like subset, n=2060) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic Regression | 64.37 | 23.85 | 0.28 | 0.64 | 13.60 | 17.43 | 90.7 |
| LinearSVC | 65.13 | 43.50 | 12.29 | 27.65 | 32.70 | 41.91 | 98.7 |
| Random Forest | 64.29 | 23.03 | 0.02 | 0.04 | 13.01 | 16.68 | 91.1 |
| XGBoost | 66.01 | 30.67 | 0.78 | 1.75 | 18.31 | 23.47 | 61.2 |
| libinjection | 61.72 | 12.63 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 6.74 | 8.64 | 80.3 |

**How to read these numbers (put this in the paper, not just the table):**
- CSIC's `Anomalous` class is not SQL injection: it also contains XSS, buffer overflow, information gathering, file disclosure, CRLF injection, and valid requests with typos. 22.0% of anomalous requests have no query/body value at all (attack is in the URL path, e.g. `.bak` probing), so a value-level SQLi detector cannot see them. Low recall/F1/accuracy against this label therefore does NOT mean SQLi is being missed.
- CSIC has no per-attack labels. As a rough proxy I flagged anomalous requests whose values match SQL syntax by a fixed regex (`SQLISH` in experiments.py, written before the models were scored and not tuned): 8.2% of anomalous and 0.0% of valid requests match. Recall on that weak subset is the last column. It is a weak label, not ground truth, and the regex overlaps with what the model learned.
- 55.6% of valid requests carry no values (static pages) and are trivially negative; the 'FPR (valid w/ fields)' column removes them.
- The few false positives on valid traffic are random-looking generated passwords/names (RF e.g. `2ef4n4o7ar`, `lin?6`; XGBoost e.g. `F*ino`, `eXc971+Bl5`). XGBoost and LinearSVC are clearly worse than Random Forest on valid traffic here.
- Domain shift: CSIC is Spanish-language e-commerce traffic with Latin-1 percent-encoding; the training data is English/synthetic.
